newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker, focus on Friday data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker, focus on Friday data.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Tuesday with investors defensive and trading thin ahead of Friday's keenly anticipated employment reports for Canada and the United States, analysts said.

"You've seen a very weak day in the U.S, with some hedge fund selling there. That's trickled over," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett. "You still have a few accounts sitting on the sidelines not wanting to commit on direction ahead of Friday's data."
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$1.30 to C$108.25 to yield 7.290 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.79 percent. The spread between the two benchmark bonds widened to 50 basis points from 45 basis points at the close of trading on Monday.

"There's no buyers in a very thin market, a small amount of selling right across the curve and nobody to buy it and offset it. The market's pretty nervous ahead of Friday's data," said one Toronto-based bond trader.

Both Canadian and U.S. bonds were defensive during the session amid concern about Friday's data. The reports coming out of Washington and Ottawa were seen as having the potential to affect bond prices sharply.
Analysts said the weakness of bonds should be taken in stride since markets were thin because many investors were refraining from active trading until Friday.

Canada's underperformance relative to the United States in today's session was seen as unusual given a sharp rally in the Canadian dollar. The dollar rallied almost a full Canadian cent stronger, prompting the Bank of Canada to intervene and sell the currency for U.S. dollars.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.85 to C$102.35 to yield 6.670 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 3/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 12 basis points from six basis points at the close of trading on Monday.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.88 percent against the U.S. bill, which yielded 5.16 percent.
